baseline.holdoutRule: The v1-v15 holdouts were promoted to regression after evaluation. The asymmetric v16 release thresholds were frozen in the runner and baseline documentation before the v16 sources were selected. The exposed v15 positive miss remains development evidence and cannot release the revised candidate. Every complete run fails before any model call when two declared sources reach 0.995 perceptual similarity. The two v16 holdouts are previously unused real-network visuals selected, pixel-reviewed, truth-labelled and frozen before either was submitted to the production or candidate profile: one recent video frame shows a readable Singapore Deposit Mark and a visibly present linear product barcode on the same individual bottle; one real return-machine photograph hides the individual container inside the aperture, so marks printed on the machine cannot establish that container's eligibility. They are developer-visible, non-adaptive holdouts rather than an independently sealed or blinded evaluation set, and must not be used to revise and re-score the same candidate.

invariants: Only containers carrying the BCRS Deposit Mark are eligible for a refund.
The refund is S$0.10 per eligible container.
Containers without the mark remain recyclable through blue bins or other recycling stations.
The scheme product-approval guide distinguishes the product barcode from the separate square 2D traceability code printed on some approved labels.
